messages:
Alex: CI promo blocked — staging canary (canary-3) failing on artifact extract across multiple runners. deploy-bot created a hold.

DeployBot: Promote paused by deploy-bot at 1719876543. Reason: artifact-extract-fail (tar EOF) on 4/6 staging jobs. Link: https://ci.redwood/integrations/5678 :warning:

Priya: seen similar last month after we changed cache TTL. Fail log looks like truncated wheel file during tar extract on runner-42 and runner-11.

Michael: quick paste from runner-42 logs:
```
ERROR: tar: unexpected EOF
E: failed to extract /tmp/artifacts/redwood_lib-1.3.2-cp39-manylinux2014_x86_64.whl: truncated file (expected 1234567, got 934512)
HTTP GET s3://redwood-ci-wheels/2026/03/15/wheels/1234.part: 200 OK, Content-Length mismatch
```

Sara: S3 GET/content-length mismatch suggests a bad multipart upload or a cache serving stale partial object. Could also be a proxy returning truncated body.

CI-Runner-Bot: re-run job command: `/ci retry integrations/canary-3 --only artifacts` queued 4 jobs.

Priya: I pulled the wheel locally and it looks truncated too. Key includes the cache stamp that rotated at 03:02AM UTC. I'm +1 to re-upload the wheel and invalidate the cache key.

Alex: We need a decision — do we pin the canary to previous successful image to unblock the release window, or do a reupload and wait for verification? Change window ends in ~45m.

Michael: We can fast-unblock by pinning to `service-image@sha256:deadbeef...` (last good digest) and let the reupload happen in parallel. I can open a short-lived rollout to that digest. Deploybot update would be manual promote.

Sara: Steps I propose: 1) manual promote to pinned digest to unblock. 2) Michael kicks off artifact reupload + run `ci-artifact-verify` against 3 runners. 3) once green, we retarget canary to new digest and remove pin. 4) follow-up postmortem about cache TTL/multipart failures.

Priya: One caveat — the edge cache TTL might still hand out partial objects for a bit. We should set a new cache key for the reupload (append current commit sha). Also add `NO_CACHE=1` to the verify job to ensure fresh fetch.

DeployBot: Manual promote API: `/deploy promote --env=staging --service=canary-3 --digest=sha256:deadbeef --reason="pin to known-good image to unblock"` (requires two approvals).

Alex: Approval: I'm +1. @Priya can you +1?

Priya: +1.

Michael: I'll run the reupload now and open the promote. Starting upload to s3 with `multipart_threshold=10MB` and explicit checksum verification. Will post progress.

sre-bot: Observability: there was a spike of S3 5xx errors in us-west-2 ~30m ago, storage team got paging alert. Might explain partial writes. Ticket #ST-1432 opened.

Sara: I'll execute the manual promote once deploybot shows the promote request and approvals. Also I'll add a temporary rollback playbook in release notes in case the reupload doesn't finish before the window. :thumbsup:

Michael: upload finished, checksums match locally. Triggering verify job with `NO_CACHE=1` now. Link: https://ci.redwood/jobs/verify-7890

CI-Runner-Bot: verify-7890 started on runner-9, runner-21, runner-42.

Alex: timeline: pin now (T+0), verify expected T+8m, retarget canary T+20m if green. If any verify fails, revert pin and run rollback plan.

Priya: noted. Also adding a short-term monitoring alert to watch for `artifact.extract.errors` rate increase during rollback window.

DeployBot: Promote request created: ID 8342. Waiting for 2 approvals.

Sara: approved.

Alex: approved.

DeployBot: Promote executed: canary-3 -> sha256:deadbeef at 1719876609. Promote comment: pinned to unblock release window.

Michael: verify jobs all passed. Green across 3 runners. I'll coordinate retarget to new digest after 10m smoke.

Priya: logging follow-up: I'll add cache key suffix and a health-check to the artifact upload pipeline. We'll schedule a postmortem with storage team since they had 5xxs.

Alex: OK — unblocking done. Postmortem owners: Priya (artifact pipeline) + Michael (uploader) + Sara (release owner). We'll document in release notes and link the storage ticket. Thanks everyone. :raised_hands:
